response: Yes, eligibility for a chemotherapy protocol is a good prognostic factor for invasive bladder cancer after radical cystectomy. This is because patients who are eligible for chemotherapy tend to have fewer comorbidities and better overall health, which can contribute to a more favorable outcome. Additionally, the ability to tolerate chemotherapy suggests a lower risk of treatment-related complications and a better likelihood of completing the full course of treatment, both of which are associated with improved survival rates.
